title: Interviewing Yiyang Zhuge (Zhong Shu) - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Tyler Cowen defends proceeding with an interview of Chinese intellectual Yiyang Zhuge despite plagiarism accusations, arguing interestingness trumps guilt for guests, and analogizes her case to hosting DeepSeek's CEO given that DeepSeek distilled heavily from Anthropic's Claude.

insights.claim: Cowen's default reaction to hearing a potential guest did something wrong is to ask whether they are interesting to talk to, having previously hosted CEOs, a former CIA head, Sam Bankman-Fried, and a convicted murderer without regret.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: A stated editorial principle prioritizing insight over reputational purity, relevant to how his interviews should be read.
insights.quote: Are they interesting to talk to?

insights.claim: Cowen notes plagiarism and other standards in China differ substantially from those in the United States, which shapes how he weighs the accusations against Zhuge.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: A reminder to calibrate cross-cultural norm judgments when assessing Chinese figures and institutions.
insights.quote: standards in China, including for plagiarism, are very different than in the United States
insights.locator: The relevant facts here still are being disputed

insights.claim: Cowen states it is well known that DeepSeek and other Chinese AI models distilled a lot from Anthropic's Claude, calling it a terms-of-service violation and, in economic terms, a depredation of serious magnitude.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Frames Chinese model distillation from US frontier labs as a material economic harm, relevant to IP and AI-competition risk.
insights.quote: it is pretty well known that DeepSeek (and other Chinese AI models) distilled a lot from Anthropic’s Claude. That is a violation of terms of service

insights.claim: Cowen says he would be delighted to host DeepSeek CEO Liang Wenfang without obsessing over the distillation issue, treating the alleged IP violation as no bar to a valuable conversation.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Signals continued openness to engaging Chinese AI leaders despite IP controversy.
insights.quote: I still would be delighted to have Liang Wenfang on the show, and I would do so without obsessing over the issue of distillation.
